gloss: be strong, prevail; strength, might; strong, fierce
summary: To be strong and to prevail: a hand strong against an enemy, wisdom stronger than ten rulers, man who must not prevail against God. The noun עֹז is strength, above all Yahweh's own, by which he divided the sea and led his people (Exo 15:13; Psa 74:13), and which he gives to them and to his king, so that his people say “Yah is my strength and my song” (Exo 15:2; Isa 12:2; Psa 118:14) and the righteous run into a “tower of strength”, the name of Yahweh (Pro 18:10). The adjective עַז is strong (a people, a wind, the waters, love “strong as death”) and, of anger, a king or a face, fierce and hard; “to make the face strong” is to be brazen (Pro 7:13; 21:29). Arabic ʿazza “be mighty; overcome”, Ugaritic and Phoenician ʿz, Ge'ez ʿazzaza and the Aramaic עַזִּיז “strong” share the sense; Akkadian ezzu “fierce” the hard side of it.

words.summary: About a hundred times, three in four in the Psalms and the prophets and most of those of Yahweh: his strength, the strength he gives, and Yahweh himself as his people's strength. Also spelled עוֹז. The brief's count includes eight tokens of the name עֻזִּי (Uzzi), which is spelled the same as עֻזִּי “my strength”.

senses.definition: The strength a man, a woman, a nation, a beast or a city has: what it acts with and trusts in; with גְּאוֹן “the pride of”, the strength a people boasts in and Yahweh breaks.

evidence.note: “How have you helped the one without power (כֹחַ), saved the arm without עֹז!”: strength set beside כֹּחַ.
“She girds her loins בְעוֹז, and makes strong (וַתְּאַמֵּץ) her arms.”
“עֹז and splendour are her clothing.”
Of Leviathan: “In its neck lodges עֹז.”
“March on, my soul, with עֹז.”
“David danced before Yahweh with all עֹז.”
“David and all Israel were playing before God with all עֹז.”
“A wise man is בַּעוֹז, and a man of knowledge makes power (כֹּחַ) strong.”
“I will break the pride of your עֹז, and make your heavens like iron”: the strength Israel trusted in, broken by Yahweh.
The sanctuary is “the pride of your עֹז, the desire of your eyes”, to be profaned.
“The pride of her עֹז shall come down”, of Egypt; so Ezk 30:18.
Of the land of Israel: “the pride of her עֹז shall cease.”
“An adversary … shall bring down your עֹז from you, and your palaces shall be plundered.”
The vine had “rods of עֹז for the sceptres of rulers”; now “no rod of עֹז” (Ezk 19:14).
Of Moab: “How is the rod of עֹז broken, the staff of beauty!”
“In the day I called you answered me; you made me bold in my soul with עֹז.”
The Levites and priests praised Yahweh “with instruments of עֹז”: loud instruments.

senses.gloss: stronghold, strong place; (with מִגְדַּל, קִרְיַת) a strong tower, a strong city
senses.definition: In the construct phrases “tower of strength” and “city of strength”, and alone: a strong place to flee into; often of Yahweh or his name as that refuge.

evidence.note: “There was a מִגְדַּל־עֹז in the midst of the city, and all the men and women fled there and shut themselves in.”
“A מִגְדַּל־עֹז is the name of Yahweh; the righteous runs into it and is set on high.”
“You have been a refuge (מַחְסֶה) for me, a מִגְדַּל־עֹז from the face of the enemy.”
“The wealth of the rich is his קִרְיַת עֻזּוֹ; the ruin of the poor is their poverty.”
The rich man's wealth is his strong city, “and like a high wall in his imagination”: a false refuge set beside the true one of Pro 18:10.
“A brother offended is harder to win than a קִרְיַת־עֹז.”
“A wise man scales the city of the mighty and brings down the עֹז of its confidence.”
“You are my strong refuge (מַחֲסִי־עֹז).”
“In the fear of Yahweh is a strong confidence (מִבְטַח־עֹז), and to his sons there shall be a refuge.”
“By your favour you made my mountain to stand עֹז.”
Tyre's “pillars of your עֹז shall go down to the ground.”
“Though she should fortify the height of her עֹז”, of Babylon.

senses.definition: Yahweh's own might, shown in creation, the sea, the storm and his acts for Israel; he is clothed and girded with it, and it dwells in his sanctuary.

evidence.note: “You led in your kindness the people you redeemed; you guided them בְעָזְּךָ to your holy habitation.”
“You divided the sea בְעָזְּךָ; you broke the heads of the sea monsters on the waters.”
“Once God has spoken, twice I have heard this: that עֹז belongs to God.”
“Yahweh reigns; he is clothed with majesty; Yahweh is clothed, he has girded himself with עֹז.”
“You crushed Rahab like one slain; with the arm of your עֹז you scattered your enemies.”
“You are the God who does wonders; you made known your עֹז among the peoples.”
“By the greatness of your עֹז your enemies cringe before you.”
“He led out the south wind by his עֹז”, bringing the quails.
“The downpour, the downpours of his עֹז.”
“With him are עֹז and sound wisdom.”
“The hand of our God is on all who seek him for good, and his עֹז and his anger against all who forsake him.”
“Who knows the עֹז of your anger?”
“Awake, awake, put on עֹז, arm of Yahweh”: his arm clothed with strength; so Zion is told, “put on your עֹז” (Isa 52:1).
“Yahweh has sworn by his right hand and by the arm of his עֹז.”
“I have seen you in the sanctuary, to see your עֹז and your glory.”
“עֹז and beauty are in his sanctuary”; 1Ch 16:27 “in his place”.
“Praise him in the expanse of his עֹז.”
“His majesty is over Israel, and his עֹז in the skies.”
“Rays from his hand, and there the hiding of his עֹז.”
“Arise, Yahweh, to your rest, you and the ark of your עֹז”; so 2Ch 6:41.
Of the ark taken at Aphek: “he gave his עֹז into captivity, and his beauty into the hand of the adversary.”
“Seek Yahweh and his עֹז; seek his face continually”; so Psa 105:4.

senses.gloss: strength given by Yahweh; Yahweh as one's strength
senses.definition: The strength Yahweh gives to his people and his king; with a suffix, Yahweh himself is “my strength”, “their strength”, the one in whom strength is found.

evidence.note: “עָזִּי and my song is Yah, and he has become my salvation”: Israel's song at the sea; the same words in Isa 12:2 and Psa 118:14.
“Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust and not be afraid, for עָזִּי and my song is Yah Yahweh.”
“Yahweh will give עֹז to his people; Yahweh will bless his people with peace.”
“The God of Israel, he gives עֹז and power to the people.”
“Blessed is the man whose עֹז is in you.”
“Yahweh is עֻזִּי and my shield; in him my heart trusted, and I was helped.”
“Yahweh is their עֹז, and he is the stronghold of salvations of his anointed.”
“God is to us a refuge and עֹז, a help in distress, very present.”
“עֻזּוֹ, to you I will watch, for God is my high place”: the refrain that Psa 59:18 sings as “עֻזִּי, to you I will sing”.
“I will sing of your עֹז, and shout for joy at your kindness in the morning.”
“Sing aloud to God our עֹז.”
“The rock of עֻזִּי, my refuge, is in God.”
“Yahweh, עֻזִּי and my stronghold (וּמָעֻזִּי) and my refuge in the day of distress.”
“Yahweh, Lord, the עֹז of my salvation.”
“Only in Yahweh, one shall say of me, are righteousness and עֹז.”
“Turn to me and be gracious to me; give your עֹז to your servant, and save the son of your handmaid.”
Hannah: “Yahweh will judge the ends of the earth, and give עֹז to his king, and exalt the horn of his anointed.”
“Yahweh, in your עֹז the king shall rejoice.”
“The rod of your עֹז Yahweh will send out from Zion: rule in the midst of your enemies.”
The ruler from Bethlehem “shall stand and shepherd בְּעֹז of Yahweh … for now he shall be great to the ends of the earth.”
The servant: “my God has become עֻזִּי.”
“You are the glory of their עֹז, and by your favour our horn is exalted.”
“The עֹז of the king loves justice.”

senses.definition: In “give to Yahweh glory and עֹז”, the strength that worshippers acknowledge and declare to be his; Psa 8:3, quoted by Jesus, is read in the Greek as praise.

evidence.note: “Give to Yahweh, sons of the mighty, give to Yahweh glory and עֹז.”
“Give to Yahweh, families of the peoples, give to Yahweh glory and עֹז”; so 1Ch 16:28.
“Give עֹז to God.”
“From the mouth of babes and sucklings you have founded עֹז because of your adversaries, to still the enemy.”

Jesus quotes Psa 8:3 of the children crying “Hosanna to the son of David” in the temple: “out of the mouth of babes and sucklings you have perfected praise (αἶνον).” The strength founded is the praise that silences the adversary.

senses.definition: With פָּנִים: the hard, bold set of the face, which wisdom changes.

evidence.note: “A man's wisdom makes his face shine, and the עֹז of his face is changed.”
“Be strong in the Lord and in the might of his strength (τῆς ἰσχύος αὐτοῦ)”: the strength found in Yahweh, as Psa 84:6.
“Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power and riches and wisdom and strength (ἰσχύν)”: strength ascribed, as Psa 29:1.

evidence.locator: Ezr.8.22; Job.12.16: עֹז → κράτος

evidence.note: Mary: “He has shown might (κράτος) with his arm”, the arm of Yahweh's strength of Psa 89:11 and Isa 51:9.
“To whom is the glory and the might (τὸ κράτος) for ever”: the ascription of Psa 29:1.

evidence.locator: Psa.8.3, עֹז → αἶνον

evidence.note: Jesus quotes Psa 8:3 in the Septuagint's words: “you have perfected praise (αἶνον).”

parallels.note: “Song”: the fixed pair “my strength and my song is Yah”.
“Glory”: ascribed to Yahweh with עֹז, and seen with it in the sanctuary.
“Beauty, glory”: in the sanctuary with עֹז, and given with it into captivity in the ark.
“Salvation”: Yahweh's strength is his people's salvation.

phrases.gloss: my strength and my song is Yah

words.summary: About twenty-five times. The brief's 38 tokens include 14 of the place name עַזָּה Gaza, filed here by spelling, which is not of this root (see the note). Strong in force, and, of anger, a ruler or a face, fierce and unyielding; its fixed partner in that sense is קָשֶׁה “hard”.

senses.definition: Of a people, an enemy, a lion, a wind, the sea's waters, a city or a border: having force that is hard to withstand.

evidence.note: The spies: “But עַז is the people who dwell in the land, and the cities are fortified and very great.”
“What is sweeter than honey, and what is עַז than a lion?”; the riddle, “out of the עַז came sweetness” (Jdg 14:14).
“The ants are a people not עָז, yet they prepare their food in the summer.”
“He delivered me from my enemy עָז, and from those who hated me, for they were stronger (אָמְצוּ) than I”; so 2Sa 22:18.
“The strong (עַזִּים) gather against me, not for my transgression.”
“I will make the pride of the strong to cease.”
“He makes destruction flash against the strong, and destruction comes upon the fortress.”
“Therefore a strong people will glorify you.”
“For the border of the sons of Ammon was עַז.”
“Yahweh drove the sea by a strong east wind all night.”
“Who makes a path in the mighty waters (בְמַיִם עַזִּים)”; so Neh 9:11.
“We have a strong city (עִיר עָז־לָנוּ); he sets salvation for walls and rampart.”
Reuben, “excellence of dignity and excellence of עָז”.
“Love is עַזָּה as death; jealousy is hard (קָשָׁה) as the grave”: strong as death, which none withstands.

senses.definition: Of anger, a king, a face or an appetite: fierce and unyielding, hard toward others; “fierce of face” is the face that shows no regard.

evidence.note: “Cursed be their anger, for it is עָז, and their wrath, for it is hard (קָשָׁתָה).”
“I will give Egypt into the hand of a hard (קָשֶׁה) lord, and a fierce king (מֶלֶךְ עַז) shall rule over them.”
“A nation עַז פָּנִים, which will not lift up the face for the old, nor show favour to the young.”
“At the latter end of their kingdom … a king עַז־פָּנִים, understanding riddles, shall stand up.”
“The poor speaks entreaties, but the rich answers עַזּוֹת”: harshly, the opposite of entreaty.
“A gift in secret pacifies anger, and a bribe in the bosom strong wrath (חֵמָה עַזָּה).”
The watchmen are “dogs strong of appetite (עַזֵּי־נֶפֶשׁ); they do not know satisfaction.”

evidence.locator: Jdg.14.14, 18; Pro.21.14: עַז → ἰσχυρός

evidence.note: “How can one enter the house of the strong man (τοῦ ἰσχυροῦ) … unless he first binds the strong man?”

evidence.locator: Deu.28.50; Isa.56.11, עַז → ἀναιδής/ἀναίδεια; Dan.8.23 ἀναιδὴς προσώπῳ

evidence.note: “Because of his shamelessness (ἀναίδειαν) he will rise and give him”: the hard face of עַז פָּנִים turned to bold persistence in asking.

parallels.note: “Hard”: the fierce anger, ruler or jealousy is also hard.

opposites.note: “Entreaties”: the poor man's pleading set against the rich man's harsh answer.

words.gloss: be strong, prevail; (hiphil) make the face strong, be brazen
words.summary: Twelve times: ten qal, “be strong” and “prevail against”, and two hiphil, the face made strong, of the shameless. Two qal tokens (Isa 30:2; Psa 52:9) stand beside מָעוֹז “stronghold, refuge” and may be of עוּז “take refuge” (see the note).

stems.gloss: be strong; prevail (against); make oneself strong in

senses.definition: Of Yahweh's hand, of God, of wisdom, of the springs of the deep: to be or show itself strong.

evidence.note: “To you is an arm with might (גְּבוּרָה); תָּעֹז your hand, your right hand is high.”
“Your God has commanded your strength (עֻזֶּךָ); עוּזָּה, God, you who have worked for us”: be strong, show your strength.
“Wisdom תָּעֹז for the wise more than ten rulers who are in the city.”
“When he made firm (בְּאַמְּצוֹ) the skies above, when the springs of the deep grew strong (בַּעֲזוֹז).”

senses.definition: With עַל, or alone: to be stronger than another and hold him down; in prayer, that man may not prevail against God.

evidence.note: “Yahweh gave Cushan-rishathaim into his hand, וַתָּעָז his hand against Cushan-rishathaim.”
“וַתָּעָז the hand of Midian against Israel”, so that Israel made dens in the mountains.
“Arise, Yahweh; let not man (אֱנוֹשׁ) prevail; let the nations be judged before you.”
The king of the south “will cast down myriads, but he will not prevail.”

senses.gloss: make oneself strong in, be secure in
senses.definition: With בְּ: to find one's strength or safety in something trusted in place of God.

evidence.note: “To be strong (לָעוֹז) in the stronghold of Pharaoh, and to take refuge (וְלַחְסוֹת) in the shadow of Egypt.”
“Behold the man who did not make God his stronghold, but trusted in the abundance of his riches, and יָעֹז in his destruction.”

senses.gloss: make the face strong, put on a bold face
senses.definition: With בְּפָנָיו or פָּנֶיהָ: to harden one's face, showing no shame; of the wicked and the adulteress.

evidence.note: The adulteress “seized him and kissed him; הֵעֵזָה פָנֶיהָ and said to him …”
“A wicked man הֵעֵז with his face, but the upright, he considers his way.”

evidence.locator: Jdg.3.10, וַתָּעָז → ἐκραταιώθη; Psa.9.20 → κραταιούσθω; Psa.89.14 → κραταιωθήτω

evidence.note: “The child grew and became strong (ἐκραταιοῦτο) in spirit.”
“To be strengthened (κραταιωθῆναι) with power through his spirit in the inner man.”

words.summary: Three times: twice Yahweh's might told in his works, once the force of battle poured out with his anger.

senses.definition: The might shown in what Yahweh has done, which his people recount to the next generation.

evidence.note: “Recounting to the generation to come the praises of Yahweh, וֶעֱזוּזוֹ, and his wonders that he has done.”
“They shall speak of the might (וֶעֱזוּז) of your awesome deeds.”

senses.definition: The fierce force of war, poured out on Israel with Yahweh's anger.

evidence.note: “He poured on him the heat of his anger וֶעֱזוּז of battle; it set him on fire round about, but he did not know.”

words.summary: Twice: of Yahweh, the king of glory, and as a noun of a mighty army.

senses.definition: Strong in battle: Yahweh coming in as the king of glory, and the might of Pharaoh's army that he quenched.

evidence.note: “Who is this king of glory? Yahweh עִזּוּז and mighty (וְגִבּוֹר), Yahweh mighty in battle.”
“Who brings out chariot and horse, army וְעִזּוּז; they lie down together, they shall not rise.”

evidence.locator: Psa.24.8, עִזּוּז → κραταιὸς

evidence.note: “Humble yourselves under the mighty (κραταιὰν) hand of God.”

words.summary: Twice, in the two lists of unclean birds, after the נֶשֶׁר and the פֶּרֶס: a large bird of prey, which kind is not known. Its link to the root's sense is not clear; it may be named for its strength, and Arabic has a word of the root for an eagle, but this rests on little.

senses.gloss: a bird of prey, not to be eaten
senses.definition: One of the great birds of prey listed as detestable, not to be eaten.

evidence.note: “These you shall detest among the birds … the eagle (נֶשֶׁר), the פֶּרֶס, and the עָזְנִיָּה.”
The same three, at the head of the list.

cognates.gloss: be mighty, strong; overcome, conquer; be hard, difficult; (ʿizz) might, strength; (ʿazīz) mighty, invincible; rough
cognates.note: The same two sides as the Hebrew: strength and the prevailing it gives (“he overcame him”, as qal Jdg 3:10; Psa 9:20), and hardness (ground, manner). Arabic shows ʿ (not ġ) behind ע and z (not ḏ) behind ז.

evidence.note: “He was, or became, mighty, potent, powerful, or strong … He resisted, or withstood … عَزَّهُ He overcame him, or conquered him”; the proverb مَنْ عَزَّ بَزَّ “he who overcomes takes the spoil”.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2031, art. عز, عِزٌّ (n28917)
evidence.note: “Might, potency, power, or strength.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2032, art. عز, عَزِيزٌ (n28923)
evidence.note: “Mighty, potent, powerful, or strong … rough in manners … indomitable; invincible.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2033, art. عز, مَعْزُوزَةٌ (n28934)
evidence.note: Of ground: “hard, or firm”.

cognates.gloss: an eagle (in one verse, on a disputed reading)
cognates.note: The feminine of “mighty” used of an eagle in a verse of Abū Kabīr al-Hudhalī; other readings of the verse have other words. A thin lead for עָזְנִיָּה as “the strong (bird)”.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2032, art. عز, عَزِيزَةٌ (n28925)
evidence.note: “An eagle: so in a verse of Aboo-Kebeer El-Hudhalee: but as some relate that verse, it is عَزِيبَة.”

cognates.note: Ugaritic keeps ʿ and ġ, z and ḏ apart: ʿ and z, as Arabic.

SEM000630 ʿzz [strong] V, UGC001093 ʿz [strong]
x000002950, ʿzz, be(come) strong (V), form tʿzzk

cognates.note: Phoenician has the Hebrew's noun and adjective together, with the noun's “bulwark” of a god beside the Hebrew's “Yahweh is my strength”, and names formed as the Hebrew ones are: ʿzbʿl “Baal is my bulwark” or “Baal is strong”, ʿzmlk “Milk is strong”.

p. 362, ʿZBʿL, ʿZMLK, ʿZMLQRT (personal names)

cognates.note: Ge'ez has merged ġ into ʿ and ḏ into z, so it does not show which older sounds stand behind the letters.

evidence.note: “validum, fortem, robustum esse vel fieri”; ዐዚዝ “validus, fortis, potens”; ዕዝዝ “robur, potentia, fortitudo”.

evidence.locator: SEM000630 ʿzz [strong] V, GEZ000907 ʿazzaza [strong] V

cognates.gloss: strong, intense; (ithpaal) become strong, be defiant
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic of the Targums and Talmud. The Targum of Isa 7:18 uses the plural construct עֲזִיזֵי.

evidence.locator: s.v. עַזִּיז (P00409), citing Snh. 7a and Targ. Is. VII, 18; s.v. עֲזַז ch. (P00404), Ithpa. אִתְעַזַּז

doctrine.statement: At the sea Israel sang, “My strength and my song is Yah, and he has become my salvation” (Exo 15:2), for he had divided the sea by his strength and guided them by it to his holy habitation (Psa 74:13; Exo 15:13). The same words are sung again by those he will save in the day of Isaiah's prophecy, “Behold, God is my salvation … for my strength and my song is Yah Yahweh” (Isa 12:2), and by the one who says “I shall not die, but live” (Psa 118:14, 17). “Power belongs to God” (Psa 62:12); he is girded with it (Psa 93:1); and he gives it: “Yahweh will give strength to his people” (Psa 29:11; 68:36). “Blessed is the man whose strength is in you” (Psa 84:6), whose strong tower is the name of Yahweh (Pro 18:10), against those whose strong city is their wealth (Pro 10:15; 18:11) or who make themselves strong in Pharaoh's stronghold (Isa 30:2), and the man who “did not make God his stronghold, but trusted in the abundance of his riches” (Psa 52:9). Israel's own strength, the pride of it, Yahweh breaks (Lev 26:19; Ezk 33:28), and the prayer is “Arise, Yahweh; let not man prevail” (Psa 9:20). From the verses: strength belongs to God, and a man has it only as God gives it; the one who trusts in his own, or in another man's, is brought down.

Hannah's song ends, “Yahweh will judge the ends of the earth, and give strength to his king, and exalt the horn of his anointed (מְשִׁיחוֹ)” (1Sa 2:10). The king rejoices in Yahweh's strength (Psa 21:2); Yahweh is “the stronghold of salvations of his anointed” (Psa 28:8); the servant says “my God has become my strength” (Isa 49:5), and Paul applies the next verse, the light to the nations, to the preaching of Jesus (Act 13:47). To the one he tells to sit at his right hand, whom Jesus and the apostles show to be Jesus himself (Mat 22:44; Act 2:34–36; Heb 1:13), Yahweh says, “the rod of your strength Yahweh will send out from Zion: rule in the midst of your enemies” (Psa 110:1–2). The ruler from Bethlehem (Mic 5:1, applied to Jesus' birth in Mat 2:6) “shall stand and shepherd in the strength of Yahweh, in the majesty of the name of Yahweh his God … for now he shall be great to the ends of the earth” (Mic 5:3). From the verses: the anointed king rules by strength that Yahweh his God gives him, not strength of his own; his rule is from Zion and reaches to the ends of the earth, as the angel promised Mary, “the Lord God will give him the throne of his father David” (Luk 1:32).

The ark is called “the ark of your strength” in the prayer at its bringing into the house, “Arise, Yahweh, to your rest, you and the ark of your strength” (Psa 132:8; 2Ch 6:41). When Israel took it into battle as a charm and it was captured, the psalm says Yahweh himself “gave his strength into captivity, and his beauty into the hand of the adversary” (Psa 78:60–61; 1Sa 4:3–4, 11, 21–22): the strength was his to give up, not Israel's to command. When David brought it up he “danced before Yahweh with all strength” (2Sa 6:14), but when Uzzah put out his hand to it, Yahweh struck him (2Sa 6:6–7), and David learned that it was to be carried as Yahweh had commanded (1Ch 15:13–15). From the verses: Yahweh's strength was present with the ark, but it was never Israel's to use as they would; it was with them as they honoured him.
